The Series

Come in… and welcome.

In 1974, when network radio drama was thought to be gone forever, one man brought it back — seven nights a week.

Himan Brown — a giant of radio’s golden age, creator of Inner Sanctum and a producer of thousands of broadcasts — persuaded CBS Radio to try something audacious: a new hour of mystery, horror, science fiction, and adventure drama, every single night.

Each episode began with the slow creak of a heavy door and the voice of host E. G. Marshall (with Tammy Grimes hosting the final year) inviting listeners in. For nine seasons, the series gave a new generation classic adaptations — Poe, Shakespeare, the great mystery writers — alongside original plays, performed by one of the finest repertory companies ever assembled for radio.

When the series ended in 1982, its episodes survived largely as off-air recordings made by devoted fans. The performances endure. They deserve a home worthy of them.

“I am E. G. Marshall, inviting you to return to our Mystery Theater for another adventure in the macabre.”

The words that closed every broadcast

The App · Core Listening Experience

An archive you can hold in your hand.

Built to the standard the material deserves: fast, quiet, and focused entirely on the listening — making one of the greatest radio drama collections ever produced more accessible, discoverable, and enjoyable for listeners, researchers, educators, and fans.

Complete episode library

Browse and explore the entire collection through a modern archive interface — the series as it unfolded, season by season from 1974 to 1982, each episode with its own artwork, original air date, and synopsis.

More than episodes — the whole story behind them.

A recording alone is only half the inheritance. The app preserves the people, the production, and the history around the performances.

The Mission

Built as a gift, not a product.

This independent, non-commercial passion project exists for one reason: so that these performances, and the legacy of the man who created them, are never lost.

I’m Scott Ketterer, a retired UX designer and lifelong admirer of classic radio drama. I built this application alone, as a volunteer, out of gratitude for the hours of wonder Himan Brown gave listeners like me.

I am seeking no money, no ownership, and no control. My hope is that the app finds its permanent home with the people who already steward this legacy — the Brown family and the Radio Drama Network, and the archives at the City University of New York. Whatever arrangement best serves preservation is the arrangement I want:

A blessing

Simply knowing the project has the family’s goodwill, and guidance on how it should respectfully present the series.

A collaboration

Working together — so that pristine archival recordings, as they are released, could reach listeners through the app each week.

A full transition

Donating the app, its design, and its episode library outright, with my help for as long as it’s useful, then stepping aside entirely.

For listeners & fans

The complete series, finally gathered in one place — a pleasure to explore, stream, and return to night after night.

For researchers

A searchable, richly documented catalog of a landmark American broadcast series — by title, cast, writer, and theme.

For educators & students

Radio drama as literature — with production history, cast and crew profiles, and the story of the series built right in.

Begin the Conversation
